title: AgentForge: Execution-Grounded Multi-Agent LLM Framework for Autonomous Software Engineering
key_points: AgentForge is a multi-agent LLM framework with five roles (Planner, Coder, Tester, Debugger, Critic) that requires every code change to pass sandboxed Docker execution before propagation.
The framework uses dual retrieval: episodic memory of past solved tasks and a live repository index of the current codebase, both stored in ChromaDB.
AgentForge reports 40.0% resolution on SWE-bench Lite (300 tasks), versus 14.0% for a single-agent GPT-4o baseline, 12.0% for ReAct, and 18.1% for SWE-agent (published result).
Ablations on 100 tasks show removing any agent reduces resolve rate, with the Tester and Debugger contributing the largest gains and the full pipeline at 42.0%.

Error analysis of 30 failed tasks attributes most failures to faulty localization (40.0%), with ineffective patches, cognitive deadlocks, and environment issues making up the rest; the full pipeline costs about 2.7 times the single-agent baseline per task.

entities.name: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

unclear_sections: The Figure 4 caption describes resolution vs. retries, but its displayed values (about 28% to 40%) and the 'diminishing returns after N = 2' claim are only partly consistent with the text, which states 'diminishing returns beyond two retries'.

Figure 6 caption repeats the text of Figure 5 ('Resolve rates across ablation conditions') even though the figure shows error-type trajectories across debug iterations, so the caption does not match the figure.
Table II lists 40.0% for AgentForge under a 'fixed execution budget', while the ablation's full pipeline is 42.0% on a different 100-task subset, so the numbers are not directly comparable.
The Proposition 1 testable prediction (a 7B model with execution feedback beating a 70B model) is stated but not tested in the experiments.

The paper says the Critic verdict is binary, but the evaluation protocol and the 'Full pipeline' cost figures are not fully explained, and the ablation's 'w/o Debugger' value appears as 31 in Table III and 27.0% in Figure 5.
